Project Description:
Location: Kamal Ataturk Avenue, Gulshan

Year: 2016

Status: Completed

Client Name: Al Haj Abdul Hadi

Project Descriptions:

Hadi Tower at Kamal Ataturk Avenue, Banani is an outcome of rational design approach in a challenging urban setting. The surrounding area of Banani is a busy commercial area in Dhaka, occupied by compact built forms. The trapezoidal site is accessed by the Kamal Ataturk Avenue at the south with an adjacent lake to the west. The thirteen-storied building provides office space with relevant modern amenities and varied open spaces like garden, roof deck and terraces. The LEED Gold certified office building possesses sustainable features including sophisticated façade, solar panel, maximum daylight efficiency.

The building and its amenities are woven into the urban fabric of upscale Gulshan – Banani neighborhood. Entrance of the building features a double height space with vegetation in the front, providing the entrants with a congenial ambiance. Aluminum louvers in the south façade renders horizontality for the building that make it congruent with the surrounding urban context. Vertical fins juxtaposed with the horizontal members make the façade well proportioned. The louvers filter light into the interior workspace, minimizes solar glare and heat gain yet floor-to-ceiling glass optimizes daylighting and offer pleasant views of the cityscape.

Project Description:
Project : Teach For Bangladesh Headquarter
Location : 210/A-2 Bir Uttam Mir Shawkat Sarak, Dhaka
Built-up Area : 10853 sft.
Cost of Project : (US$) 94,920.00

Studio Dhaka Ltd. was handed the challenge to create a more minimalist yet brighter headquarter for TFB, featuring collaborative open-plan workspace. Also, since TFB is a donor-based welfare organization, there were fund limitations due to the charitable nature of their business. As a consequence, the concept of the project goes completely “against the wind”: A low-lying building constructed by materials of lowest possible cost. Studio Dhaka Ltd. followed a design philosophy that quite resonates with the Bangladeshi design aesthetics, with rooms that are typically light, airy and bright, with modern furnishings and natural materials, especially wood to complete the style of cool, calm and uncluttered working spaces.

Low energy consumption was another goal of the project, making utilization of the shadows of the existing trees mandatory. As a result, the pods have been arranged in an alternative manner on the opposite sides of the circulation. Through this thoughtful journey, the concept of the whole project evolved as “Weaving the Nature”.

Project Description:
Architectural photography assignment for Roofliners Studio of Architecture, the visionary designers behind JATRA’s transformed home in Banani, Dhaka. 🌿✨

This project beautifully captures the essence of sustainability, craftsmanship, and a deep connection to nature. Roofliners reimagined the space as an architectural patchwork—blending memories, upcycled materials, and modern functionality.

Our photography highlights the intricate details of this transformation, from the maze-like interiors to the open-air multipurpose hall, and the serene rooftop restaurant, Jatra Biroti.

📍 Location: Banani, Dhaka
